resale_co.name: Certificate of Occupancy (CO), Sales
resale_co.lead_time: 48 hours notice is required for the inspection; the application and fee must be in before an inspection is scheduled.
requirements: House numbers 5 inches high and visible from the street
GFI protected outlets within 6 feet of a water source and on all exterior outlets
Fire extinguisher mounted in the kitchen
Appliances installed properly and working, no extension cords; exhaust fan over the stove (ductless hood allowed) and anti-tip bracket on the stove
Adequate electric, heating and plumbing service; two separate outlets in each habitable room
Bathroom vented or with a working window
Screened window in each room; all windows working with locks; exterior doors and hardware working
Handrails on steps with more than 3 risers; rails around landings or porches 30 inches or higher
Water heater relief valve piped to within 6 inches of the floor; emergency shut-off at the top of the stairs for a basement heater
In-ground pool fenced at least 4 feet high with a self-latching gate
No work done without permits and no open construction permits
Well water test, chimney inspection and smoke/CO inspection must pass

fees.label: Certificate of Occupancy for a sale (initial inspection and one follow-up)

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill in the Township of Pilesgrove Application for Certificate of Occupancy (CO), Sales Only (revised 5/13/2025) and submit it with the fee to the Zoning & Housing Office; the office form records payment by cash or check. The owner or agent then calls to schedule the inspection (48 hours notice). Office hours are Monday and Wednesday 8:30 am to 2 pm; inspections 12 pm to 2 pm.

resale_co.notes: The Township posts a CO application for sales only (revised 5/13/2025) and a separate one for rentals; the Township Committee approved updated sales and rental CO applications and the inspection checklist on February 24, 2026. The sales form fee covers the initial inspection and one follow-up; later visits are $75 each. The checklist says residential CO inspections are $50.00. A well test, chimney certificate and smoke/CO certificate are needed before the CO is issued. The Township does not inspect septic systems and does not issue temporary COs. A web search summary of Chapter 64 (ecode360, not opened and not quoted here) suggested a housing certificate may be issued within 90 days after the passing inspection; this is not confirmed from an official page. The Housing Officer email zoning@PilesgroveNJ.org comes from the mailto link on the Zoning & Housing page. Rentals also need a lead-safe certificate (homes built before 1979) and proof of liability insurance; those are rental-only items.

requirements: Smoke alarms must be UL listed, less than 10 years old and 10-year sealed battery units; wired or interconnected systems must stay hardwired and interconnected
CO alarms on every occupiable level including the basement, within 10 feet of any sleeping area
Homes with a generator, solar panels or battery backup need a warning label within 18 inches of the main electrical panel and the electric meter
The Township CO checklist still lists a fire extinguisher mounted in the kitchen

authorities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the NJ DCA Fire Safety portal (Certificate of Smoke Alarm, Carbon Monoxide Alarm, and Secondary Power Source Identification Label Compliance). Pay by e-check or credit card before submitting; a valid email address is required. The certificate is emailed once the application is submitted, the fee is paid and any required inspections are done. Homes heated by electricity with no CO alarm requirement should also email BFCE_CSDCMAC@dca.nj.gov.

fire_cert.notes: State records say the NJ DCA Division of Fire Safety is Pilesgrove's fire code enforcing agency (LEA registry code S), mark Pilesgrove "SC" (the state issues smoke certificates) on the July 17, 2026 state towns list, and name NJ Division Fire Safety for smoke detector compliance in the fire directory (listed there under code 1709). The DCA online smoke application's own fire district feed lists Pilesgrove as State jurisdiction and not smoke-certificate exempt, so Pilesgrove can be selected in the state's online application. However, on February 10, 2026 the Township Committee appointed Leroy Pierce as "Fire Inspector for CO Requirements" and on February 24, 2026 approved a "Certificate of Smoke Alarms and Carbon Monoxide Alarms Checklist", and the Township's CO application requires a smoke/CO certificate before the CO is issued. A web search summary of Township Code Chapter 64 (ecode360, not opened) described a Township Fire Safety Inspector who performs the smoke alarm, CO alarm and extinguisher certifications for 1-2 family homes. So it is not settled whether the Township inspector or the DCA issues the certificate for a sale; both are listed. The DCA fees are the state's own published online fees. The Township smoke info sheet (undated) names the secondary power source label that replaced the extinguisher in state law (P.L.2025, c.19), but the Township CO checklist still lists a fire extinguisher mounted in the kitchen.

other_items.label: Well water test
other_items.detail: A well certificate / passing water test is needed before the CO is issued.

other_items.label: Chimney certificate
other_items.detail: A chimney certificate is needed before the CO is issued.

other_items.label: Septic
other_items.detail: The Township does not inspect septic systems as part of the CO; a septic inspection is recommended but not required by the state.

other_items.label: No open permits
other_items.detail: The CO checklist checks for work done without permits and open construction permits.

open_questions: Who issues the smoke/CO certificate for a Pilesgrove sale: the Township Fire Inspector for CO Requirements (appointed Feb 2026) or the NJ DCA (state lists)? If the Township, what is the fee?
How long is the Pilesgrove sales CO valid? (A search summary of Chapter 64 mentioned 90 days; not confirmed from an official source.)
